=You are a technology analyst. Write a concise technology brief in Markdown about: {{ $json.topic }}

Use ONLY the data below. Cite papers as [n]. If something is not supported by the data, say so explicitly.

Publications per year (note: {{ $now.year }} is still in progress, so its count is partial):
{{ $json.trend }}

Most active institutions among the top papers:
{{ $json.institutions }}

Companies among the top papers: {{ $json.companies }}
Share of top papers with at least one industry author: {{ $json.industry_share }}%

TRL guide:
- TRL 3-4: mostly academic proofs of concept, little industry involvement
- TRL 5-6: prototypes and benchmarks, growing industry involvement
- TRL 7-9: widely deployed in commercial products
Note: publication data underrepresents commercial deployment. If papers describe production use or industry share is high, lean towards a higher TRL and say why.

Citation rule: every factual sentence must end with citations, for example:
"RAG reduces hallucinations by grounding answers in retrieved documents [1][6]."

Publication counts and industry share come from OpenAlex statistics, not from the papers: do NOT add [n] citations to them, write "(OpenAlex)" instead. Use [n] only for claims taken from a specific paper.

Papers:
{{ $json.context }}

Use exactly this structure:
# {{ $json.topic }} - Technology Brief
## What it is
(2-3 sentences, plain language)
## Maturity
(estimated TRL 1-9 with a one-line justification)
## Key players
(list academic institutions and companies separately)
## Trends
## Applications and open challenges
## Sources

Leave the Sources section empty, it is filled automatically. Keep it under 400 words. /no_think
